oczekiwana_odpowiedz:
The line through $\mathbf{a} - 2 \mathbf{b} + 3 \mathbf{c}$ and $2 \mathbf{a} + 3 \mathbf{b} - 4 \mathbf{c}$ can be parameterized by
\begin{align*}
&\mathbf{a} - 2 \mathbf{b} + 3 \mathbf{c} + t((2 \mathbf{a} + 3 \mathbf{b} - 4 \mathbf{c}) - (\mathbf{a} - 2 \mathbf{b} + 3 \mathbf{c})) \\
&= (1 + t) \mathbf{a} + (-2 + 5t) \mathbf{b} + (3 - 7t) \mathbf{c}.
\end{align*}To get an expression of the form $p \mathbf{b} + q \mathbf{c},$ we want the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ to be 0.  Thus, we take $t = -1,$ which gives us $-7 \mathbf{b} + 10 \mathbf{c}.$  Hence, $(p,q) = \boxed{(-7,10)}.$

[AI]:
To determine the constants \( p \) and \( q \) such that the vectors 

\[
\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{a} - 2 \mathbf{b} + 3 \mathbf{c}, \quad \mathbf{v} = 2 \mathbf{a} + 3 \mathbf{b} - 4 \mathbf{c}, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbf{w} = p \mathbf{b} + q \mathbf{c}
\]

are always collinear, we need to find a relationship among these vectors. Vectors are collinear if one is a scalar multiple of the others, or if the determinant of the matrix formed by these vectors is zero.

We can express the condition of collinearity using the determinant of a matrix formed by these vectors. We can set up the following matrix:

\[
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & -2 & 3 \\
2 & 3 & -4 \\
0 & p & q
\end{bmatrix}
\]

The vectors are collinear if the determinant of this matrix is zero:

\[
\text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
1 & -2 & 3 \\
2 & 3 & -4 \\
0 & p & q
\end{bmatrix} = 0
\]

Calculating the determinant, we can expand it along the first row:

\[
= 1 \cdot \text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
3 & -4 \\
p & q
\end{bmatrix} - (-2) \cdot \text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
2 & -4 \\
0 & q
\end{bmatrix} + 3 \cdot \text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
2 & 3 \\
0 & p
\end{bmatrix}
\]

Calculating each of these 2x2 determinants:

1. For the first determinant:

\[
\text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
3 & -4 \\
p & q
\end{bmatrix} = 3q - (-4)p = 3q + 4p
\]

2. For the second determinant:

\[
\text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
2 & -4 \\
0 & q
\end{bmatrix} = 2q - 0 = 2q
\]

3. For the third determinant:

\[
\text{det} \begin{bmatrix}
2 & 3 \\
0 & p
\end{bmatrix} = 2p - 0 = 2p
\]

Putting it all together, we have:

\[
\text{det} = 1(3q + 4p) + 2(2q) + 3(2p) = 3q + 4p + 4q + 6p = 7q + 10p
\]

Setting the determinant to zero for collinearity:

\[
7q + 10p = 0
\]

From this equation, we can express \( q \) in terms of \( p \):

\[
7q = -10p \implies q = -\frac{10}{7}p
\]

To find a specific ordered pair \( (p, q) \), we can choose \( p = 7 \) (a convenient choice) which gives:

\[
q = -\frac{10}{7} \cdot 7 = -10
\]

Thus, the ordered pair \( (p, q) \) is:

\[
(p, q) = (7, -10)
\]

Finally, we can express the answer in the required format:

\[
\boxed{(7, -10)}
\]
